test_title: PYST 23: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 14 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: How many times may the President of India ask the Prime Minister to have an executive recommendation reconsidered by the Cabinet?

options.text: It is at the President's absolute discretion without limits.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Only once**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The President of India has the constitutional authority to return an executive recommendation to the Prime Minister for reconsideration by the Cabinet, but this can only be done **once**.
 
• This authority is granted under **Article 78** of the Indian Constitution, which outlines the duties of the Prime Minister in advising the President.
 
• If the Cabinet reaffirms its decision after reconsideration, the President is bound to accept the recommendation and act accordingly.
 
• This constitutional mechanism ensures a balance between the executive's decision-making power and the President's oversight role.
 
• The provision highlights the President's role as a constitutional head, who must act on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 78 of the Indian Constitution**

 
 
• It defines the Prime Minister's duties concerning communication between the President and the Council of Ministers.
 
• It mandates the Prime Minister to keep the President informed of all decisions of the Cabinet related to the administration of India.
 
• The article ensures the President is aware of the governance and policy decisions while maintaining a ceremonial role.
 
 
 
• **Role of the President in Indian Parliamentary Democracy**
 
 
• The President is the constitutional head of state and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• The President's role is largely ceremonial, with real executive power resting with the Prime Minister and the Cabinet.
 
 
 
• **Reconsideration Mechanism**
 
 
• The mechanism allows the President to return legislative and executive proposals for reconsideration.
 
• It is a tool to ensure thorough deliberation by the Cabinet, especially in cases of national importance.
 
 
 
• **Checks and Balances**
 
 
• India's parliamentary democracy incorporates checks and balances to prevent the misuse of power.
 
• The President's ability to seek reconsideration is an example of such a safeguard.
